newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke sees further good progress.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke sees further good progress.

text.p: British betting and hotel company Ladbroke Group Plc posted a 34 percent increase in its 1996 pretax, pre-exceptional profits to 163 million pounds, saying it expects to make further good progress during 1997.

"Our two core businesses have performed well, we have completed our exit from retailing and commercial property and net debt has more than halved since 1993," said chief executive Peter George in a statement.
Hilton International increased trading profits by an underlying 20 percent to 160.2 million, and the betting and gaming division grew profits by 46 percent to 84.9 million.

Ladbroke and Hilton Hotels Corp agreed to reunite the Hilton hotels brand worldwide for the first time in 32 years in January. Previously HHC had the rights to the Hilton name in the United States and Ladbroke owned them in the rest of the world.
Ladbroke's retail betting business in Britain showed a marked recovery despite the 8.0 million cost associated with jockey Frankie Dettori's seven winners at an Ascot race meeting in September.

Net debt fell by 315.6 million to 707.7 million, reducing the interest charge by 25.8 million to 70.3 million. At its peak three years ago the company was crippled by debt of 1.6 billion in the midst of a deep recession in the property market.

Exceptional items amounted to 103.8 million including 52.3 million arising from the group's exist from commercial property -- 16.0 million includes the cost of settling the Paris Hilton rent dispute and 15.4 million was for the adjustment to the price of DIY retailer Texas Homecare sold to J. Sainsbury two years ago.
Analysts forecast group profits in the 155-165 million pounds ($266.1 million) range. The shares rose 6-1/2p to 233p in early trade. ($ = 0.620 British Pounds)
